title: Multi-vendor contributor roster: validate, merge, export
scenario: Two CSV vendor exports (one with a UTF-8 BOM) and a JSON dump are validated row by row, inactive people are dropped, and duplicates are merged by email (latest update wins, source priority 1 breaks ties, skills unioned). The roster is then exported as JSON. Test 3 checks summary counts and the exported timestamps.

verified.why_correct: Stripping 'mailto:' looks like it might mangle addresses, but the README requires it, and only a leading prefix is removed. Lower-casing the whole address is also what the spec asks for.

Returning None instead of raising looks like a swallowed error, but check_row turns None into the `unparseable date` rejection the README asks for. The four formats match the README exactly, including the bare date (midnight) and month/day/year.

bugs.title: CSV opened without BOM handling
bugs.old: with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
bugs.new: with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
bugs.symptom: Every test file fails. Test 1: vendor_a shows accepted 0 / rejected 11 / inactive 0, and every vendor_a row is rejected as 'missing email'. Test 2: duplicates is 3 instead of 6, dev/gus/noa are missing, ana has hours 28 and skills ['spark', 'sql'] (vendor_b only). Test 3: python count 4, IL and SE missing, ana's timestamp is 2026-02-20T10:00:00.
bugs.why: vendor_a.csv starts with a UTF-8 BOM. Read as plain utf-8, the first header becomes '\ufeffemail', so row.get('email') is None for every vendor_a row and all 11 are rejected as `missing email`. vendor_b has no BOM and is unaffected.
bugs.unblocks: All vendor_a contributors (ana's merge, dev, gus, noa, kim's tie). It also exposes B2.
hints: Every vendor_a row is rejected as missing email, yet the file plainly has emails. Print the keys of one parsed row.
Look at how read_csv_source opens the file, and at the first bytes of vendor_a.csv.
probes: Why was only the first column affected?
Why is utf-8-sig safe for files that have no BOM?

bugs.title: String 'FALSE' treated as active
bugs.symptom: Masked by B1 (vendor_a rows are all rejected). Once B1 is fixed: Test 1 shows vendor_a accepted 8 / inactive 0, Test 2 has extra ben@x.io and leo@x.io in the roster, and Test 3 gains GB, NG, 'java' and a third 'spark'.
bugs.why: bool() of any non-empty string is True, so vendor_a's 'FALSE'/'false' rows count as active. Only vendor_a uses string flags (vendor_c uses JSON booleans and vendor_b has no column), so the problem stays hidden while vendor_a is fully rejected.
bugs.unblocks: vendor_a inactive count and the roster membership (ben, leo).
hints: After the encoding fix, ben and leo appear in the roster. What does their `active` cell say?
Look at how parse_active treats string values.
Restore the string branch: value.strip().lower() in TRUTHY.
probes: Why couldn't you see this until vendor_a rows were being read?
Why did vic (vendor_c, active: false) stay inactive the whole time?

bugs.title: Merged skills not de-duplicated
bugs.old: skills=sorted({s for r in group for s in r.skills}),
bugs.new: skills=sorted(s for r in group for s in r.skills),
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_records: merged people repeat skills (ana `['python', 'spark', 'sql', 'sql']`, gus `['python', 'python']`, cara/mia/raj likewise). Test 3 test_skill_counts: python 11, sql 6, labeling 2.
bugs.why: Without the set, the skills from every duplicate row are simply concatenated, so people with more than one row get repeated skills (gus: python, python; ana: sql, sql). skill_counts counts list entries, so it is inflated too (python 11 instead of 8).
bugs.unblocks: Test 2 records for merged contributors, and the Test 3 skill counts.
hints: Which contributors have a skill listed twice? What do they have in common?
Look at how merge combines skills across a person's rows.
Use a set comprehension inside sorted(): sorted({s for r in group for s in r.skills}).
probes: Is `sources` safe from the same issue? Why?

bugs.title: Blank skill entries kept after split
bugs.old: return [text(s).lower() for s in items if text(s)]
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_records: dev `['', 'python']`, fay `['']`, uma `['', 'ml', 'python']`. Test 3 test_skill_counts gains a `'': 3` entry.
bugs.why: "".split(";") is [""] and "python;".split(";") ends with "", so a blank cell or a trailing separator produces an empty-string skill. The spec drops empty entries.
bugs.unblocks: Test 2 records (fay, dev, uma) and the '' key in Test 3 skill_counts.
hints: Some contributors have a skill that is an empty string. Look at their raw skills cells.
What does str.split return for an empty string or a trailing separator?
Filter out blanks: `... for s in items if text(s)`.
probes: Why did zoe (a JSON empty list) not get an empty skill?
What would "".split() (no argument) have returned instead?

bugs.title: Timestamp ties go to the least trusted source
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_records: cara becomes `{'name': 'Cara D.', 'country': 'US', 'hours': 35}` (vendor_c) instead of Cara Diaz / MX / 40, and kim gets vendor_a's hours 15 instead of 18. Test 3 test_countries: MX missing, US 2.
bugs.why: Priority 1 is the most trusted, so on an updated_at tie the lower number has to win. max() over (updated_at, priority) picks the higher number, so cara takes vendor_c's name/country/hours and kim takes vendor_a's hours.
bugs.unblocks: Test 2 records for cara (and kim once B1 is fixed), and the Test 3 country counts.
hints: cara's name and country come from vendor_c. Compare the two cara rows: which fields are equal?
Check how pick_winner breaks a tie, against the priority convention in sources.json.
Use -r.priority in the key (or min with a reversed date).
probes: Why did kim only show this problem once vendor_a was read correctly?
Why do mixed timestamp formats (2026-01-20T10:00:00 vs 2026-01-20 10:00) still tie here?

bugs.title: Export serialises datetimes with str()
bugs.symptom: Test 3 only, test_export_timestamps: every timestamp has a space instead of 'T' (`'2026-03-01 09:30:00'` vs `'2026-03-01T09:30:00'`).
bugs.why: `str(datetime)` uses a space separator ('2026-03-01 09:30:00'), not the ISO-8601 'T' the spec requires. json.dumps hands every datetime to `_encode`, so every exported timestamp has the space.
hints: The exported timestamps have a space where the spec has a 'T'. What turns a datetime into a string here?
Follow the `default` hook of json.dumps in export_roster into `_encode`.
In `_encode`, return `value.isoformat()` instead of `str(value)` for datetimes and dates.
probes: Why doesn't json.dumps raise on the datetime values?
Why is this only visible in test_3_export, even though updated_at is used in merging?

context_qa.q: What does ingest() return, and in what order are sources read?
context_qa.a: A tuple (per_source, rejected, roster, duplicates). Sources come from sources.json with lower-cased names and are processed in sorted order: vendor_a, vendor_b, vendor_c. Each row goes through check_row, and accepted Records are merged at the end by dedupe.merge.

context_qa.q: How does read_source decide how to read a file?
context_qa.a: By suffix: .json goes to read_json_source (json.load of a list), and anything else to read_csv_source (csv.DictReader). Both wrap each row as RawRow(source, row_number_from_1, dict_of_fields).
One of ('rejected', reason), ('inactive', None) or ('ok', Record). Checks run in order: missing email, invalid email, unparseable date, invalid hours, then active.

context_qa.q: What are the first bytes of vendor_a.csv?
context_qa.a: EF BB BF, the UTF-8 byte-order mark, followed by the header line `email,name,country,skills,hours_per_week,updated_at,active`. vendor_b.csv starts directly with `name,email,...`.

context_qa.q: Which emails appear in more than one accepted row?
context_qa.a: In the source data: ana (vendor_a, vendor_b), cara (vendor_b, vendor_c), gus (twice in vendor_a), kim (vendor_a, vendor_b), mia (vendor_b, vendor_c) and raj (vendor_b, vendor_c). cara's and kim's pairs have identical updated_at values.

context_qa.q: How is the export string produced?
context_qa.a: export_roster sorts the roster by email, turns each Contributor dataclass into a dict with vars(), and calls json.dumps with indent=2 and sort_keys=True. The `default` argument handles values json can't encode natively, such as datetime.

context_qa.q: Where are skill_counts and countries computed?
context_qa.a: In reports.build_report, with collections.Counter over the merged roster's values: each contributor's skills list for skill_counts, and each contributor's country for countries. Both are returned sorted by key.
